entries.name: Independent roulette-wheel destroy/repair selection
entries.description: Destroy and repair operators are sampled independently with probabilities proportional to their current weights.

entries.name: Segmented reaction-factor weight adaptation
entries.description: Average segment performance is exponentially blended into historical operator weights.

entries.name: Novel-solution outcome scoring
entries.description: Selected destroy and repair operators receive sigma-tier rewards only when the candidate is novel under the supplied solution comparer.
entries.formula: \begin{aligned}\rho(y)&=\sigma_1\ \text{if novel global best},\\\rho(y)&=\sigma_2\ \text{if novel accepted improvement},\\\rho(y)&=\sigma_3\ \text{if novel accepted non-improvement},\\\rho(y)&=0\ \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}

entries.name: Geometric simulated-annealing acceptance
entries.description: Improving/equal candidates are accepted; worsening candidates use a Metropolis probability with geometric cooling.

entries.name: Pair-coupled destroy/repair adaptation
entries.description: Learns joint pair performance instead of independent destroy and repair weights.
entries.formula: Pair-coupled adaptation requires a separate joint state and changes the canonical independent-selection controller, so it is reserved for Advanced ALNS.

entries.name: Alternative ALNS acceptance criteria
entries.description: Alternative reusable acceptance mechanisms remain composition-compatible but are distinct from the canonical simulated-annealing default.
entries.formula: Alternative acceptance criteria are composition-compatible but remain distinct from the canonical Ropke-Pisinger simulated-annealing default.

entries.name: Contextual or learning-based operator selection
entries.description: Contextual bandit and learned policies replace the canonical historical roulette controller.
entries.formula: Learning-based operator choice is architecturally compatible but is not part of the 2006 ALNS stable identity.
